commonPrompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / production game sprite concept sheet.
Generate ONE separate image for ONE sphere family in ECHO SPHERE, visually matching the supplied REAL Unity render reference. The reference is a STYLE AND CORE/ORBIT IDENTITY reference, not an edit target. These are proposed in-game-readable native vector designs, not promotional illustrations.
STYLE LOCK: very compact flat 2D technical silhouettes, hairline bright neon outlines, nearly black interior plates, restrained narrow glow, tiny white and secondary-color inset details. Keep the small luminous round sphere core and simple thin elliptical orbit identity exactly as in the reference; change its family hue only. The core can retain its existing simple soft gradient; all mechanisms must be completely FLAT without volumetric shading. NO 3D render, extrusion, bevels, metallic shading, isometric depth, perspective guns, long barrels, large effects cloud, decorative rune art, arena backgrounds, or cinematic lighting. Must be realistic to reconstruct using retained Unity meshes and separate rigid parts. No physically thick tubes. No redesign of the base core/orbit concept.
LAYOUT: clean dark navy-black background, portrait contact sheet, exactly THREE columns and FOUR rows, twelve distinct designs total. Each column is one IV branch and its own three VII finals. Top row IV branches, next three rows their VII finals IN SOURCE ORDER. Spacious even grid like reference; consistent core size in every cell. Display whole sphere plus compact mechanism(s), never weapon-only. VII variants must be visibly richer and have DISTINCT mechanical silhouettes, not recolor-only or almost-identical IV copies. Add split cheeks, fins, articulated shutters, coils, plates or lenses that have understandable roles, at least six extra small parts on VII, while retaining compactness. Parts should clearly be separable for translation/rotation animation; bilateral parts are mirrored. These are still images, do not draw animation arrows.
TEXT: clear small white Russian sans-serif cell captions, EXACT names below, "IV ·" top row; "VII ·" all other rows, using only the final suffix after •. Big Russian family title at top. Footer "КОНЦЕПТ · НЕ ВНЕДРЕНО". No stats, fictitious numbers, gameplay UI, additional rows or extra panels.
MECHANICAL SEMANTICS: use the existing branch/final descriptions ONLY to motivate the look. They are not requests to create new abilities. Differentiate control, network, impact, splitting, draining etc via mechanical detail. Do not replace all sphere families with an identical forward gun. Use radial emitters for field families, orbiting satellites for Orbital, directional optical modules for Prism/Void as appropriate.

Gravity branch: four or six fine inward-curving ribs, different delicate hooks/retaining microtabs/paired impact flaps on finals. Living Network: thin trace links with tiny pinhead nodes, accelerator tiny fins, overflow staggered relay tags, synchronicity matched microcouplers.

families.prompt:
EDIT this orbital sheet: keep title, Russian captions, dark background, flat neon vector line style, 3 columns x4 rows, core size, colors and twin ellipse concept. COMPLETELY REPLACE every small gun-like satellite. The satellite IS a contact melee weapon itself. NO gun bodies, muzzles, sockets resembling barrels, cylinders, projectile emitters, aimed optics or central forward gun. Use solid flat cutting wedges, paired cutting fins, edged crescent plates or impact paddles; their small connecting pivot is inside and the damaging blade edge/tip is OUTSIDE. EVERY point must face RADIALLY AWAY from the central core, toward the nearest outer edge of the orbit. Do NOT orient all satellites right, and do NOT orient their tips tangent to the orbit or toward the center. Across one sphere: right satellite points right, top satellite points up, left satellite points left, bottom points down, diagonal satellites point out diagonally.
Correct the count and scale: first row IV has EXACTLY FIVE small satellites total (2 on inner ellipse,3 outer). All VII cells have EXACTLY EIGHT total (4 inner,4 outer), except bottom-left VII Dance Swarm has NINE (4inner,5outer). Satellites may be slightly smaller so all fit with clear space between them. No large repeated gun modules. Distinct branches must be identifiable by their cutting-edge shape and tiny articulated details: streamlined echo/dance blades, segmented resonance/protection guard blades for Halo, sharp impact/echo blades for Blade. Retain richer VII, modest local glow and all12 captions. The core and combat paths remain fully visible. These are flat 2D melee satellite assemblies, no 3D bevels.
